walkthroughs.body_html:
The big formula:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

If you run 100 m in 20 s, your speed = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 m/s.

You can rearrange the formula too:

Distance = Speed × Time
Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Common speed units:

m/s - science standard.
km/h - car speed limits in most countries.
mph - used in UK and USA roads.

Roughly: 1 m/s ≈ 3.6 km/h.

So 10 m/s = 36 km/h - the speed of a fast sprinter.

Real journeys aren't constant speed - you stop at lights, slow down for corners.

Average speed = total distance / total time.

Drive 60 km in 1.5 hours: average = 40 km/h, even if you sometimes went 70 or 0.

That's the value that shows up on satnavs as your overall trip speed.
